receipt.uninstall: revokes host registration and assets; independent service remains ready
receipt.scope: disposable local API fixture; no browser, provider access or production mutation

coverage: The official released Portal installed the released Beta.2 ZIP, deliberately paired the released Beta.2 service, then preserved an administrator-only component, disabled monitor and sealed disposable credential.

The normal installer upgraded to the released Beta.3 ZIP and service. The old token was denied, old backend authority was cleared, and a deliberate new pairing retained the same store, configuration and sealed credential fingerprints.

The normal installer rolled back to the immutable Beta.2 ZIP and service with another deliberate pairing. Configuration and sealed credentials remained byte-equivalent, and safety settings remained paused/private.
Uninstall revoked the host registration and installed assets. Portal health/account/home/queue APIs remained available and the independent Status service remained ready.
All fixture processes stopped, temporary credentials/keys were removed, and the receipt was written only after complete cleanup.
limits: The drill used the released legacy application installer and API, not the unpublished App Platform v2 production installer.
It used the published Darwin arm64 Portal and Status archives in an isolated local fixture. It did not mutate production, start a browser, contact providers or configure notification delivery.
Linux execution of the same released lifecycle helper remains covered by source tests and deployment evidence, not by this Darwin receipt.
